title: Parrot Perch Pendulum: Coffee Mug Ballistic Launch
description: A parrot perches on the rim of a giant coffee mug that acts as a pendulum. The user configures swing amplitude, release angle, gravity, air resistance, and launch force to catapult the parrot through a series of floating rings. Physics parameters must be validated and the parrot follows a realistic projectile trajectory after release.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a physics pendulum-launch simulation. Load coffeeMug.glb and Parrot.glb from shared_assets/. Scene setup: place the coffee mug (scaled 3x) suspended from a pivot point at the top of the screen by a visible rope (a thin CylinderGeometry), forming a pendulum. The Parrot model sits on the mug rim. Add a skybox-style gradient background (light blue to white) with ambient and directional lighting. Place 5 glowing torus rings at increasing distances along a parabolic arc as targets. Camera: perspective camera at z=20 looking at origin, with OrbitControls for inspection. UI panel (HTML overlay, top-left) with these validated inputs: (1) Swing Amplitude (10-90 degrees, default 45), (2) Release Angle (-80 to 80 degrees from vertical, default 30), (3) Gravity (1-20 m/s², default 9.8), (4) Air Drag Coefficient (0.0-1.0, default 0.1), (5) Launch Boost Force (0-50 N, default 15). Add a 'Swing' button that animates the mug pendulum using simple harmonic motion with the configured amplitude. Add a 'Launch' button (active only during swing) that releases the parrot at the specified release angle, applying launch boost as an impulse vector tangent to the swing arc. After release, animate the parrot along a projectile trajectory accounting for gravity and quadratic air drag each frame (Euler integration, dt from clock.getDelta). The parrot should rotate slowly during flight. Detect collisions with torus rings (distance-based, threshold 1.5 units) and flash them green on hit. Display a score counter and max distance reached. Add a 'Reset' button to return everything to initial state. Validate all parameters on input: clamp out-of-range values and show red borders on invalid fields. Use AnimationMixer to play the Parrot's flapping animation during flight.
